newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Democrats vow assembly seizure in handover.
newsitem.headline: HK Democrats vow assembly seizure in handover.

text.p: Leaders of Hong Kong's democracy movement vowed on Tuesday to force their way into parliament in a defiant protest as the world watches Britain hand the territory back to China.

It was the first hint of any potentially-violent disruption to months of careful planning for the heavily-guarded midnight ceremony and gala, attended by 4,000 VIP guests, ending 156 years of colonial rule.

Pro-democracy campaigners, who have won Western sympathy, complain that with the handover Hong Kong's democratically-elected parliament is to be scrapped and replaced by a hand-picked legislature acceptable to China.
Hours earlier authorities blocked plans for public rallies of protest by the Alliance in Support of the Patriotic Democratic Movement in China.
Then, the Democratic Party, the largest in Hong Kong, raised the stakes of protest by indicating it was prepared to defy official bans.
The party planned a bold counter-move in the small hours of July 1 to clash with the new assembly's inauguration, party vice chairman Yeung Sum said.

Yeung said activists would make speeches of protest in the doomed Legislative Council chamber. And an aide told reporters: "We will consider a non-peaceful operation, if authorities block our way in."

At midnight on June 30 thousands of dignitaries from all over the world will attend a ceremony at the nearby Convention Centre, where Prince Charles will hand Hong Kong's sovereignty back to President Jiang Zemin after 156 years of colonialism.

Representatives of the Democratic Party will attend the handover ceremony but try to steal the limelight from the swearing in of the provisional legislative council, which follows shortly after. Britain and the United States have threatened to boycott this ceremony in protest.
Civic authorities on Tuesday rejected a request by the Alliance to stage a rally in Victoria Park, named after Britain's 19th century empress.
"Our members will join the protest organised by the Hong Kong Alliance, there will be a big demonstration," Yeung said.
The Democrats have cried foul over the provisional law-making body and have tried unsuccessfully to challenge it legally.
China's Foreign Minister Qian Qichen showed Beijing was unruffled by the Anglo-American boycott.
Tung, who takes office on July 1, unveiled measures on Tuesday to dilute the presence of pro-democracy politicians in local government by appointing extra pro-China figures to local councils.
The changes complement plans to replace the elected Legislative Council with an interim China-appointed body.
Crowds were expected to gather in Chater Garden, next to the current legislative council, at 10:00 p.m. on June 30, Yeung said but gave no details of any counter-demonstration.
